historical_record.description: The Doggie Diner dachshund-head sign was put up outside the chain's restaurant at the northeast corner of Sloat Boulevard and 46th Avenue, erected at the same time as the restaurant.
The Doggie Diner restaurant building at the northeast corner of Sloat Boulevard and 46th Avenue went up in 1966, together with its sign.
The last Doggie Diner, the restaurant at Sloat Boulevard and 46th Avenue, closed in 1986; the Carousel fast-food restaurant took over the same building.
The City of San Francisco acquired the Doggie Diner sign in December 2000, after a grassroots campaign to save it.
The Doggie Diner sign blew down and was damaged in a windstorm on April 1, 2001; the Department of Public Works then restored the head and gave it a new pole.

unknowns: The restaurant and its sign are dated 1966, though 1969 is also given — the year the assessor's roll gives the building.
